summary.text: Chuck Fleischmann is the Republican U.S. Representative for Tennessee's 3rd District and won re-election on November 3, 2026.

An attorney from Chattanooga who ran a law practice with his wife before winning the seat in 2010, he serves on the House Appropriations and Science, Space, and Technology committees and chairs the Appropriations Subcommittee on Energy and Water Development.

paragraphs.text: Chuck Fleischmann was born in New York, New York, in 1962.

He earned a bachelor's degree in political science from the University of Illinois in 1983, graduating with Phi Beta Kappa and magna cum laude honors according to his official biography, and a J.D. from the University of Tennessee-Knoxville in 1986.
After law school he and his wife, Brenda, ran a law firm in Chattanooga; his official biography says they ran a small business together for 24 years.

He served as president of the Chattanooga Bar Association in 1996 and as chairman of the Chattanooga Lawyers Pro Bono Committee, and has sat on the boards of the National Craniofacial Association and the Cherokee Area Council of Boy Scouts of America.
Fleischmann won election to the U.S. House on November 2, 2010, defeating John Wolfe (D) and Savas T. Kyriakidis (I), and took office in January 2011.
In 2014 he won the Republican primary over Weston Wamp, the son of former Rep. Zach Wamp, by fewer than 1,500 votes.

He serves on the House Appropriations Committee (Subcommittees on Energy and Water Development, Labor-HHS-Education, and Defense) and the Science, Space, and Technology Committee (Energy Subcommittee); in the 119th Congress he chairs the Energy and Water Development Subcommittee.
According to his official biography, he and Brenda live in Ooltewah, Tennessee, and have three children.
He won the November 3, 2026 general election with 57.6% of the vote to Anna Golladay's 40.2%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
